audit.title: Automation Concepts

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. The page opens with navigation ("Before you explore how Chainlink Automation works… you should explore core concepts") and the Upkeeps section leads with an ambiguous pronoun: "These are the jobs or tasks that you execute onchain." Neither the term "upkeep" nor "trigger" gets a definition in the first sentence of its section.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good. 3 headings, 0 level skips, sections under 200 words, and a clean 3-item bulleted trigger list. No table where one (trigger type → use case → compatibility requirement) would extract cleanly.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Only "three types of triggers" is concrete; vague quantifier "many" present, no versions, no numeric limits, no `AutomationCompatibleInterface` method signatures.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 13 links but 12 internal and 0 to primary sources; ERC-677 links to an internal token-contracts page rather than the EIP-677 spec.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Middling. "These specific conditions are called *triggers*" is liftable; "upkeep" and "Automation Node" lack a crisp one-sentence definition near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Poor. Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable to a pure concepts page; no code expected, none present. Neutral, not penalized as a defect.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Middling. Covers the concept set but headings are concept-titled ("Upkeeps and triggers", "Automation nodes"), not phrased as the questions devs ask ("What is an upkeep?", "Which trigger type should I use?"). No FAQ or decision guidance.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; product naming ("Chainlink Automation Network", "Automation Nodes", "upkeep") is consistent. Minor: ambiguous "These" opener.

audit.summary: This is a short (261-word) conceptual overview of Chainlink Automation, introducing upkeeps, the three trigger types, and Automation Nodes. Its strength is a clean, chunkable bulleted breakdown of triggers with links out to guides; its biggest weakness is thin, non-self-contained openers ("These are the jobs...", "Before you explore...") that don't lead with liftable definitions, compounded by absent metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates). The honest verdict: structurally sound but too thin and preamble-heavy to win citations for "what is a Chainlink upkeep/trigger" queries — it defines concepts adequately but never in a first, standalone sentence an engine can quote.

recommendations.title: Lead each section with a self-contained definition
recommendations.where: "Upkeeps and triggers" and "Automation nodes" section openers
recommendations.issue: "These are the jobs or tasks that you execute onchain."
recommendations.change: Open with "An **upkeep** is a registered onchain job that Chainlink Automation executes automatically when its **trigger** condition is met." Open the nodes section with a one-sentence definition of an Automation Node before the service description.
recommendations.why: Engines lift the first sentence of a section; an ambiguous-pronoun opener is not quotable and defaults answers to generic priors.

recommendations.title: Add question-phrased headings/subheadings
recommendations.issue: concept-titled headings miss "how do I…/what is…" retrieval
recommendations.change: Add H3s or FAQ entries such as "What is a Chainlink upkeep?", "Which trigger type should I use?", "Do time-based triggers need AutomationCompatibleInterface?" (answer: no — already stated in body).
recommendations.why: Symptom/question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add a trigger comparison table
recommendations.issue: three triggers described in prose bullets only
recommendations.change: Add a table: Trigger type | When it fires | Requires `AutomationCompatibleInterface` | Example use case. Time-based = No; custom logic / log = Yes.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract decision reasons and the compatibility distinction cleanly.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, canonical URL, and `inLanguage`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Freshness and schema raise agent trust/parseability (E-E-A-T); measured facts confirm all are currently absent.

recommendations.title: Cite primary sources
recommendations.change: Link ERC-677 to the canonical EIP alongside the internal token-contracts page; link `AutomationCompatibleInterface` to its reference/source.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative references raise citation rate and attributability.

recommendations.title: Replace the vague quantifier and add specifics
recommendations.change: Drop "many more"; instead name the `checkUpkeep`/`performUpkeep` functions the interface requires and state the count of coded examples linked.
recommendations.why: Concrete parameters and named methods outperform qualitative prose in generative retrieval.

antiPatterns: Ambiguous pronoun opener: "These are the jobs or tasks…" (entity unclear until second clause).
Vague quantifier: "any one of our coded examples… and many more."
Navigational preamble as the page's first content ("Before you explore…") rather than a definition.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; confirm it lists this URL.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are template/site-level concerns; fix in the docs layout, not just this page.
Head metadata could not be verified from the provided content — pass raw `<head>` to the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
